newsitem.title: HONDURAS: ACPC regional coffee talks set for Honduran jungle.
newsitem.headline: ACPC regional coffee talks set for Honduran jungle.

text.p: Central American coffee nations of Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) will meet next Monday in the jungle Mayan resort of Copan in a routine follow-up to recent talks in Rio de Janeiro where the cartel sliced programmed exports.
Honduran coffee officials told Reuters Tuesday the regional meeting was programmed at the Rio pow-wow and one of the top items on the agenda would be to analyse figures."

Representatives from Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica will attend. Ecuador and Venezuela will also be present, given they are considered in the bloc. Colombia has been invited but confirmation is awaited, officials said.

"It is a continuation of the ACPC meeting in Rio," Fernando Montes, the head of Honduran Coffee Institute (Ihcafe), told Reuters. "It is nothing special, we will talk on a regional basis about what was decided at Rio and the situation of crops in our countries," Montes said.

"But it is an open agenda. Colombia has been invited and we are still waiting for confirmation," he said, adding he hoped ACPC Secretary-General Roberio Oliveira would also fly from London to the meeting at the world-famous ruins.
Montes said that contrary to earlier reports Mexico had not been invited. "It is not a member of the ACPC," he said.
Montes said he thought the confusion arose from the fact that following the Feb 17-18 reunion there is the annual meeting of Promecafe in Tela, Honduras, on Feb 19.
Promecafe, short for Programa Cooperativo Regional Para El Desarrollo Tecnologico y Modernizacion de la Cafecultura, is a regional coffee body promoting Latin American coffees.
Montes said Mexico had been invited to that Promecafe meeting along with Guatemala, the one rogue central American nation not taking part in the ACPC's export limits.
Osmond Maduro, the head of the Honduran Coffee Exporters Association, confirmed the Copan meeting was routine.
"The meeting was already programmed," Maduro told Reuters. "We are going to look at numbers, look at what was decided in Rio but now with new and more numbers."
Maduro said the meeting was scheduled over two days but would probably be wrapped up inside one day.
"Still, it will be interesting to analyze the market situation. All the world wants to know why prices have risen so much and we will be talking about that," he added.
ACPC decided in January in Rio to slice a further 1.3 million 60-kg bags off exports programmed by member nations for the first half of 1997.
